title: FHIR-RAG Synthetic Dataset: 200 Specialty-Medication Patients with Paired FHIR R4B Bundles, LLM and Templated Narratives, and 13,800 PSP Adherence-Indicator Questions
description:
Synthetic dataset accompanying the preprint Representation Wins on QA, Not on ML (DOI to be added; see related_identifiers).

Contents. 200 patients generated with Synthea plus a custom specialty-regimen overlay assigning each patient to one of three complexity tiers (Tier 1: single long-acting injectable; Tier 2: cyclic on/off regimen; Tier 3: multi-drug biologic + oral + PRN). Each patient is rendered in three parallel representations:

  • FHIR R4B bundle (MedicationRequest, MedicationAdministration, Medication, CarePlan, Encounter, Patient, Practitioner), validated against the reference R4B conformance validator with zero mandatory-element failures.
  • LLM-generated narrative (Llama 3.3-70B via Groq, temperature 0.0, fixed prompt hash 518bc71d87b7; 100% prompted-entity recall verified by independent programmatic audit).
  • Templated narrative (deterministic programmatic generator, no LLM; same fidelity audit, 100% recall).

The dataset further includes a 13,800-question evaluation bank across five PSP adherence-indicator families (temporal_lookup, regimen_aggregation, regimen_compliance, temporal_comparison, cross_resource), all with programmatically-computed ground truth from FHIR resources (no LLM-as-judge anywhere).

Freeze manifests. Two byte-reproducibility manifests are included: freeze.json (SHA-256 4d0da93e19c3071414ef5e1045d338104f9628842abe34f548aa050e9d0aa736; original results-freeze-v1 state) and freeze_v2.json (SHA-256 2358e8284338f5f52b66b1b9972fd8811c625cda829b0ed128c784fdf617deb7; results-freeze-v2 state including no-retrieval baseline and templated-narrative arm artifacts).

No PHI. All patient data is fully synthetic. The dataset contains no real-patient information and is suitable for unrestricted academic and commercial reuse under CC-BY-4.0.

Use cases. Reproducing the preprint results; benchmarking retrieval systems on specialty-medication adherence QA; evaluating clinical RAG architectures on temporally-grounded multi-step reasoning; training/evaluating models for FHIR-structured medication question answering.
notes: Synthetic data only; no PHI. Generated with Synthea (Apache-2.0) plus a custom specialty-regimen overlay; LLM narratives produced with Llama 3.3-70B via Groq. The full reproducibility recipe, including model identifiers and prompt hashes, is in section 7 of the accompanying preprint and in the repository docs/.
